items.title: Wilson "Willie T" Turbinton Interview, 1990-09
items.q: We all sort of embraced the idea after Earl initiated the contact with Jules Khan and the people who had the building.

ctx.x: Will you talk just a little bit about the closing of the workshop and the demise of it, and what you recollect from maybe why it closed or those kinds of things?

Well, I think one of the basic reasons that after a while we weren't able to market it as well as we could. I think that maybe if we had more people who had a serious background in writing grants and seeing the need for it, then maybe it would have survived, you know. I think Earl had a closer touch as to what was actually happening with that thing. Because to a large degree this is Earl's baby. I mean, you know, I loved the opportunity to do it, but I certainly don't want to take all the credit for making it…
How do you want the workshop remembered?
